output.title: Measure memory only if the workflow depends on it
output.body:
If you are asking about agent memory, the useful question is not “can it remember?” but “does this workflow actually need memory?” For a small business, that only matters when the same system must carry context across separate interactions: a customer asks on Monday, replies on Wednesday, and the agent should still understand the earlier request without you pasting the whole thread back in.

That is the bounded decision for a pilot. Don’t try to measure memory in the abstract. Pick one recurring workflow and define one observable test: does the agent correctly reference a prior preference, instruction, or open issue without being re-fed the full history? If it cannot, you have learned something practical. If the task is fresh each time and the input is already complete, memory may not be the thing to pay for.

The diagnostic question is simple: are your repeated tasks truly stateful, or are they just repetitive? Stateful means later steps depend on earlier ones; repetitive means each request arrives with enough context on its own. That distinction is usually clearer after ten minutes with a notepad than after ten pages of theory.

One practical next step: write down one real recurring interaction and the exact pieces of information that must carry forward. Then stop there and use that list to decide whether memory belongs in the pilot at all.
